arguments.key_record: rsi points to a 16-byte key record: +0x00 key pointer, +0x08 key length (copied wholesale into the new node with a 16-byte move)
arguments.return_value: rax = address of the mapped-value slot (node +0x18), on both the hit path and the insert path

census.direct_calls_note: 0x5f0f052 is a real e8 call instruction targeting 0x5f0e660, confirmed in objdump output; the caller function's identity was not read (only the call site was disassembled)

container_layout.this_plus_0x08: bucket count (divisor for every bucket computation)
container_layout.this_plus_0x10: list-head field (before-begin node; a slot holds this field's address when the bucket's first node is the list head)
container_layout.this_plus_0x18: element count, incremented only on insert
container_layout.this_plus_0x20: rehash-policy object, passed as the first argument to _M_need_rehash
container_layout.this_plus_0x28: field copied to a stack slot before _M_need_rehash; that slot's address is the rehash callee's third argument (a restore pointer: the callee's landing pad writes the saved value back to this+0x28)

found_path.key_check: candidate's +0x10 must equal the key length, then memcmp(key pointer, candidate +0x08, key length) must return 0; either mismatch advances the walk
found_path.return: address of the candidate's +0x18 slot, via the shared canary-checked tail
found_path.zero_next_guard: if the before-node's successor is null on the found path, control falls through to the insert path; unreachable on a consistent table (a match implies a real candidate node), recorded as defensive code, not as a behavior

hash_call.body: by contract, not read: 0x61c34a0 is the hash callee cited by the neighbouring packets; only its call site, seed and 32-bit result (kept in ebp, zero-extended for the divisions) are claimed here

in_window_calls.name: rehash callee (mapped by the neighbouring RE-001 packet)

insert_path.allocation: operator new (0x28 bytes, PLT 0x63f0dd0); the 16-byte key record is copied to node +0x08/+0x10, node +0x00 is set to 0 and node +0x18 (mapped value) is set to 0
insert_path.count: this+0x18 increments by 1 after the splice, on the insert path only
insert_path.empty_slot_arm: node becomes the list head (this+0x10 := node, node +0x00 := old head); when the old head exists, the old head's bucket slot is rewritten to the new node FIRST, then this bucket's slot is set to the head-field address -- so a same-bucket old head ends up pointing at the head field

need_rehash_call.arguments: (policy object at this+0x20, bucket count at this+0x08, element count at this+0x18, 1)
need_rehash_call.returns: al = whether a rehash is needed, rdx = new bucket count; the rdx value is moved to rsi before the test, so it is consumed only on the rehash path

insert_path.occupied_slot_arm: the slot value is re-read at insert time (0x5f0e7af): node +0x00 := before-node +0x00, then before-node +0x00 := node (spliced directly after the before-node, at the head of the bucket's run; when the slot holds the head-field address, the node becomes the new list head). The splice position comes from the slot, not from where the walk ended -- a walk that ends at a foreign-bucket node or at null still inserts after the slot's before-node
insert_path.rehash_path: when _M_need_rehash reports true, the callee 0x5f0e520 is called with (this, new bucket count, address of the stack slot holding the saved this+0x28); afterwards the bucket is recomputed as hash % new bucket count and the bucket offset is recomputed before the splice
insert_path.return: address of the new node's +0x18 slot, via the shared canary-checked tail

landing_pads.behavior: endbr64, then the exception object is kept and control jumps to the sized-delete block at 0x5f0e82c: operator delete[] (node, 0x28), canary check, _Unwind_Resume

layout_inference: this+0x00 bucket array, +0x08 bucket count, +0x10 list-head field, +0x18 element count, +0x20 rehash policy, +0x28 restore field; node +0x00 next, +0x08 key pointer, +0x10 key length, +0x18 mapped value, +0x20 hash code. The slot-as-before-node shape is observed behavior; any libstdc++-style naming for the container (operator[] shape, _Hashtable) is inference, not a claim

call_sites.note: covers the hash call (0x5f0e695) and the memcmp call (0x5f0e713); no landing pad, nothing is stored yet on this path
covers the _M_need_rehash call (0x5f0e794) and the rehash call (0x5f0e7e0); the pad deletes the freshly allocated node and resumes unwinding
covers the _Unwind_Resume call itself, with no landing pad

lsda.header: lpstart omitted, ttype omitted, call-site encoding uleb128, call-site table length 16

node_layout.plus_0x20: hash code, compared as a full 64-bit word against the zero-extended 32-bit hash

stack_slots.rsp_plus_0x00: bucket byte offset (bucket * 8), recomputed after a rehash
stack_slots.rsp_plus_0x08: saved bucket index across the memcmp call
stack_slots.rsp_plus_0x10: saved copy of this+0x28, whose address is the rehash callee's third argument
stack_slots.rsp_plus_0x18: stack canary, checked on both return paths

unknowns: the hash callee 0x61c34a0's body: cited by contract, not read in this packet
the caller function containing 0x5f0f052: only the call site was read
the exact C++ spelling of the function (operator[] shape is the reading of the single-pointer return plus zero-initialized mapped value, not a proven symbol)
whether bucket count 0 is reachable in a live table: the division has no zero guard in-window, so a zero count would fault; no live-table evidence either way

walk.advance: next := current +0x00; a null next ends the walk (insert path); otherwise the next node's bucket (its +0x20 hash % bucket count) must equal the target bucket, else the bucket's run has ended (insert path); otherwise the before-node advances to the current node and the check repeats
walk.bucket: bucket = hash32 % bucket count (64-bit division of the zero-extended hash); the byte offset bucket * 8 is kept in a stack slot for the later splice
walk.first_candidate: slot value (the before-node) is tested for null first -- a null slot goes straight to the insert path; otherwise the first candidate is the before-node's successor
walk.match_order: full hash-code compare first, then key-length compare, then memcmp on the key bytes
